”), an industry leader in the premium vapor products space, reported results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, and provided an update on recent business highlights.
Key Financial Highlights for First Nine Months 2026 (compared to first nine months 2025)
Revenue increased 19% to $11.3 million
Gross profit decreased 3% to $2.4 million
Operating loss increased 75% to $3.9 million
Key Balance Sheet Highlights as of September 30, 2026 (compared to December 2025)
Cash balance of $0.4 million, compared to $1.3 million
Total assets of $11.2 million, compared to $11.6 million
Total stockholders’ equity of $1.4 million, compared to $3.4 million
Management Commentary

“Because billions of dollars of illicit vapor products – made by Chinese manufacturers who thumb their noses at the FDA – have flooded the United States this year, Charlie’s sales and profits have taken a hit,” reported Henry Sicignano, President and CEO. “Fortunately, we have the inventory, and the opportunity, to reestablish growing, profitable sales in several states where regulatory enforcement has again become a priority. In this environment, we have redoubled our commitment to regulatory compliance as well as our initiatives to monetize the Company’s 678-SKU PMTA portfolio.”

Mr. Sicignano continued, “Big Tobacco ‘pod systems’ are outdated, provide very low puff counts, and offer few flavor choices. Charlie’s products are modern disposable products… offering much higher puff counts…
and hundreds of flavors
that adult consumers strongly prefer.

For all these reasons, we believe Charlie’s PACHA product line is the best, most robust portfolio of PMTA products in the industry and will likely represent significant value to one or more Big Tobacco strategic partners in 2027.”
As previously reported, Charlie’s has made the well-considered decision to focus intensely on the two strategic priorities that matter most to Company shareholders:

1) Management has shifted its priorities from sales of the PACHAMAMA and SBX product lines to a laser focus on the beta test pilot of PACHA age-gated disposables. The Company has already received tens of thousands of finished age-gated PACHA products in its warehouse. Management has secured test-market purchase commitments from retailers. As soon as the Company’s software licensor completes final tests of its “second generation” consumer app, Charlie’s will begin shipping the age-gated PACHA product to stores. The Company expects that Charlie’s PACHA age-gated products will be America’s
first
age-gated disposables.

2) The Company has redeployed the priorities of one of Charlie’s largest shareholders. Ryan Stump, Charlie’s co-founder and former COO, has begun work to identify and pursue strategic transactions and/or partnerships with leading global tobacco companies to significantly enhance long-term value for Charlie’s shareholders.
Regulatory Developments
FDA Enforcement Priorities Guidance

In August 2026, the FDA notified Charlie’s that certain of its PACHA products (56 SKUs) for which PMTAs have been submitted have been tentatively identified for inclusion on the FDA's public-facing webpage of products for which the FDA generally does not intend to prioritize enforcement of premarket authorization requirements — a development the Company views as highly favorable. Inclusion on the FDA’s new list of “low-enforcement priority products” does
not

, however, constitute FDA marketing authorization, preclude case-by-case enforcement, or bear on whether any PMTA will ultimately be granted. Accordingly, Charlie’s intends to continue pursuing FDA review of its pending PMTAs and to comply with all applicable requirements.
FDA has validated age-gating as a pathway for the legal sale of flavored Electronic Nicotine Delivery System (
ENDS
) products

In May 2026, the FDA granted marketing orders for four Glas Inc. pod products, including “Gold” (mango) and “Sapphire” (blueberry) flavored, age-gated pods. This landmark development validates “age-gating” as a legitimate pathway for the legal sale of flavored ENDS products in the United States. However, Juul Labs filed a patent infringement lawsuit against Glas, Inc. and, under these circumstances, Glas’ newly authorized “fruit flavored” products are unlikely to go on the market in the near term; it is likely that Charlie’s PACHA age-gated products will be America’s
first
age-gated disposables.
Business Catalysts
Charlie
s plans to begin beta testing PACHA age-gated flavored disposables.

In December 2025, the Company signed a definitive licensing agreement to commercialize the first-ever AI-powered blockchain-based age-gating system for vapor products in the United States. Scheduled to beta test this year, the PACHA test-market initiative will incorporate the age-gating system in a special line of the Company’s flavored ENDS disposables; simultaneously, Charlie’s intends to amend certain of its existing PMTAs with the FDA for PACHA brand ENDS with the youth access prevention system.

Mr. Sicignano commented, “Charlie’s plans to launch PACHA products that have not yet received final FDA authorization follows the example set by one of America’s largest tobacco companies… In recent months, RJ Reynolds' Vuse business began selling four new fruit flavor pods (berry, fresh mint, peach, and watermelon), all of which were issued FDA Marketing Denial Orders (MDOs). Given that Reynolds has demonstrated it is willing to pursue flavored ENDS commercialization strategies, before final FDA authorization, we believe the strategic calculus for Charlie’s –
and for our potential strategic partners
– has improved. Dramatically.”
Charlie
s will monetize the Company
s PMTAs through new strategic partnerships

In 2025, in three separate transactions, Charlie's sold sixteen of the Company's PACHA synthetic nicotine PMTA products and related assets for $7.5 million in cash plus a contingent one-time payment of up to $4.2 million.
In the last of the three transactions, the buyer purchased a single Charlie’s PMTA product for $1 million.

Based on these sales, taking into account the fact that Charlie’s continues to own 678 PMTA products, and considering the interest other companies have expressed in Charlie's portfolio, the Company believes Charlie's remaining PMTA products, as a stand-alone asset, could have a monetary value that significantly exceeds the Company’s current market cap.
Financial Results for the Three Months Ended September 30, 2026
Revenue:

For the three months ended September 30, 2026 revenue was $2.7 million, a decrease of $3.4 million, or 56%, compared with $6.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. This decrease was primarily due to a significant decrease in sales of the SBX product line, from ongoing inconsistency in regulatory enforcement affecting customers’ desire for non-nicotine based vapor products. The decline in sales was offset by the launch of USA-made Pachamama line and sales of Pacha disposable products that are still under substantive review with FDA.
Gross Profit:
For the three months ended September 30, 2026 gross profit was $0.1 million, a decrease of $1.5 million, or 92%, compared with $1.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.
Total Operating Expenses:

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, total operating expenses, including general and administrative, sales and marketing and research and development costs, were $1.8 million, a decrease of $0.2 million, or 10%, compared with $2.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.
Operating Loss:
For the three months ended September 30, 2026, operating loss was $1.7 million, compared with an operating loss of $0.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.
Financial Results for the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026
Revenue:

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026 revenue was $11.3 million, an increase of $1.8 million, or 19%, compared with $9.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. This increase was all due to the increase in nicotine-based product and nicotine alternative products sales. Sales of SBX, a non-nicotine, disposable vapor product which is not subject to FDA review, experienced a significant increase in the early part of 2026.
Gross Profit:
For the nine months ended September 30, 2026 gross profit was $2.4 million, a decrease of $0.1 million, or 3%, compared with $2.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
Total Operating Expenses:

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, total operating expenses, including general and administrative, sales and marketing and research and development costs, were $6.3 million, an increase of $1.6 million, or 34%, compared with $4.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
Operating Loss:
For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, operating loss was $3.9 million, compared with an operating loss of $2.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
